# Review, pass 1: secret-history-169-169

Numbering below is the new numbering (21 units); old 14 and 15 are merged into new 14, old 16-22 are new 15-21.

Counts: high 12, medium 16, low 10 (total 38 findings fixed), 7 refused.

Checked and found sound: t equals the packet words of its range in every unit; words has one entry per word; every Ming bracket in the morphs equals the packet gloss (word 117 lerün has none, as in the packet); keys are {t,l,i,n,words}; p only on unit 1, untouched.

## Findings refused

| proposal | reason |
|---|---|
| Treat Jeke-Čelen of §169 as the Tatar Jeke-Chelen of §§154-157 | The Ming gives 人名 only; here he is Atan's brother. No evidence either way; left unasserted. |
| Translate the horse names (Chaqa'an 'white') | The Ming says only 馬名; left as names. |
| Split unit 18 (21 words) or unit 14 (16 words) | Each is one syntactic sentence/chain carried to a finite verb; within the 300-520-word-part habit of the published units; splitting would break a converb chain for no gain. |
| Change ger to one English word everywhere | 'home' with the reflexive (unit 1), 'tent' elsewhere is how the glossary reads ger ('house, tent, household'); the note says so. |
| Change Cheren/Chelen in i | Published 154-157 use Chelen and Cheren as printed; kept. |
| Rework uqasuγai / odčuγ̇ui / abčira analyses | Consistent with the known glossary entries, stated as uncertain; nothing in the Ming contradicts them. |
| Touch p on unit 1, t of any unit, or the number/order of words | Not touched; t and words verified against the packet for all 205 words (one words entry per word, Ming brackets match). |

- conventions.md at publish: Names in i: Alaqchid, Narin-Kegen, Atan, Badai, Kishiliq, Jeke-Chelen/Cheren; horses Merkidai-Chaqa'an, Aman-Chaqa'an-Keger.

# Pass 2

Checked again: t equals the packet words of its range in all 21 units (205 words); one `words` entry per word; the Ming bracket on every stem morph equals the packet gloss (suffix morphs carry none, as in pass 1); keys {t,l,i,n,words}; p only on unit 1. Gloss: 42 new keys and 26 `__broaden__` keys; every key is a reader token of some `t` (R.tokens) and every token has an entry, no unused keys; each broadened entry begins with the old published entry whole + ' · ' (verified by script); each broadening is warranted by a Ming gloss or use the old entry does not carry. Dictionary forms, Ming brackets and the uncertainty flags of the 42 new entries were read against the packet and the published neighbours (tuγar-un, -daγ̇an, huja-, jer-en, nü, qaγan); no invented modern forms found.

Counts: high 0, medium 3, low 12 (total 15 fixed), 3 refused.
